title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon's algorithm with a tame-wild class walk and fixed-base tables

claims.statement: For uniform s in 1..r-1 with T=[s]P0 and the supplied powers A_i=[s^i]P0, n=2^20 (valid for every n with 2^20<=n<r; only A_d with d=2^20 and T are read), recover s with Cheon's algorithm. Since d=2^20 divides r-1, s^d lies in the subgroup E of d-th powers of F_r^* (order (r-1)/d, log2 = 234.857). Phase 1 finds v=s^d by a van Oorschot-Wiener parallel collision search with distinguished points (theta=2^-90): tame points [e]P0 and wild points [e]A_d, e in E, on classes under the six units +-lambda^i (the cube root of unity acts through the G1 endomorphism), 2^116.765 walk steps, each one F_r multiplication plus a fixed-base signed 32-bit-window multiplication (7 batched incomplete affine additions) from tables of 2^35 points; only tame-wild collisions solve and they give v exactly. Phase 2 extracts a d-th root by 20 square roots in F_r and finds the d-th root of unity by a 2^10 x 2^10 baby-step giant-step with attack-side verification [s]P0=T. Success probability at least 0.39 (Poisson tame-wild model giving 0.39, with a 10 percent step margin giving 0.45). Total work W(2^20) <= 2^119.7654 target-group-operation equivalents (1 unit = one batched incomplete affine addition = 2000 instructions), including all preprocessing (tables 2^36 units), trail starts, distinguished-point storage, overshoot, phase 2 and verification; the score submitted is 119.8. Peak memory at most 2^41.6 bytes (tables 3.3 TB plus 2^33.4 bytes of distinguished points); preprocessing at most 2^36 units, included in total work; nonuniform advice 2^0 bytes. Classical. Heuristics: the class walk with 2048 random jumps behaves like a random mapping within a 10 percent step margin (Teske 2001), uniform low bits of the canonical x-coordinate, and independent trails. The instruction ledger is analytic and not a built implementation.

experiments.purpose: Run the tame-wild class walk, exact scalar-ratio recovery of s^d and d-th root step end to end in a toy group of order about 2*10^4. This does not establish production costs, memory or success probability.
